then.text: My best customer! Laverbread's laver seaweed, picked off the rocks, boiled for hours till it's a black purée. Richard Burton called it Welshman's caviar.
Fry it in a little cake with oatmeal, next to cockles and bacon. That's a Swansea breakfast. Anything else is just toast.
Penclawdd cockles! Proper ones, the size of a thumbnail, raked off the sands this morning. Look at you. A natural.
Sit down there. Cockles, laverbread, bacon, a fried egg, a pot of tea. Proper Swansea breakfast. Then take some for the road.
Out west on the north shore of Gower, past the salt marsh. Penclawdd. Ask for Dilys on the cockle beds.

else.text: Shwmae! Laverbread, cockles, the finest stall in the market. Only I'm out of cockles, and the boy who fetches them has gone to Tenerife.
Could you nip out to Penclawdd on the Gower and fetch me a bag? Dilys on the sands will see you right. I'll do you a breakfast you'll tell your grandchildren about.

mkt_baker.text: Picau ar y maen, cakes on the stone. Flour, butter, sugar, currants, cooked on a hot bakestone. Never an oven. An oven is for English people and scones.
Diolch, bach. Eat them warm with a bit of sugar on, and don't tell your dentist.

mkt_shopper.text: I come in for a pound of cockles and come out with a Welsh cake, a bag of bara brith, a plant and a new kettle. Every week.
The roof's all glass. On a sunny day it's like shopping in a greenhouse full of gossip.
